lesson_title: Four Kinds of Work: Who Gets the Hundred Rand
hook_text: Shrink South Africa's economy to R100. The farmer who feeds us all gets... R3.
clip_script: Shrink the whole economy to a single hundred-rand note and pay the four workers their real shares. Here is the shock. The farmer — the one who feeds all sixty million of us — walks away with about three rand. The miner, from the industry that built Johannesburg, takes less than ten. The factory worker collects about twenty. And the service workers — the banks, shops, taxis, schools, hospitals — pocket roughly sixty-six rand of the hundred. But a small share is not a small importance: the farmer's three rand feeds everybody at the table. No wheat, no bread, no country.
visual_style: A hundred-rand note splitting into animated piles beside shots of a Swartland wheat field, a mine headgear, a factory line and a busy shopping centre.
pacing: Hook with the payout, count the piles, land the twist.
